recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No further core FHIR work is needed unless a future work group decision changes the examples or the base cardinality for Composition.section.title.
issue_request: The Published/Persuasive with Modification Jira issue asked whether Composition.section.title should be 1..1 when a section is present. The approved resolution was not to change core cardinality, but to add a comment explaining that sections generally SHOULD have titles, that some documents make titles unnecessary or inappropriate, and that most Implementation Guides will require section titles.
initial_application: Jira records svn revision 6195. In migrated git history, commit 9096e1f8fb40b5d7ca6e1925a15fe9db7c171141 (#7072 - add note about Composition.section.title) applied the guidance to source/composition/composition-spreadsheet.xml. The 2021 source rework in commit 33b409a4b6d544598262f2f074ebb4b6dc466157 moved the Composition definition into source/composition/structuredefinition-Composition.xml.
additional_context: Composition is active in source/fhir.ini, so source/composition/structuredefinition-Composition.xml is in current build scope. The current source has Composition.section.title as 0..1 and includes the requested guidance: sections generally SHOULD have titles, but titles can be unnecessary or inappropriate for subsections with their own distinguishing titles or single-section documents, and most IGs will make section title required. Confluence had no FHIR-7072 references, and the only directly relevant Zulip snapshot was an IPS profile question about required section titles, which does not conflict with the core guidance.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current build-scope source already implements the approved compromise for FHIR-7072, and adding another example or restating the guidance would not materially change implementer understanding.
